settings.title: Settings
settings.lookingForAnalysis: Looking for analysis options — species identification, non-bird wildlife detection, detection confidence, or GPU use? Those are chosen per run in the Analyze dialog, under “Review settings”.
settings.editor.label: Preferred Editor
settings.editor.hint: Choose which editor Kestrel should use when opening originals. “System Default” will use your OS default application.
settings.editor.customHint: Full path to an application executable (e.g. C:\Program Files\MyEditor\editor.exe or /Applications/MyEditor.app).
settings.treeScanDepth.label: Tree scan depth
settings.treeScanDepth.title: How many folder levels to scan when building the folder tree (1–6)
settings.treeScanDepth.hint: How many subfolder levels to scan when building the folder tree (1–6). Higher values may increase scan time.
settings.uiLanguage.label: Interface language
settings.uiLanguage.hint: Menus, dialogs, and buttons are shown in this language where a translation exists. Anything not translated yet falls back to English.
settings.language.label: Language (bird names)
settings.language.hint: Species names are shown in this language when a translation exists. Files, tags, and search keep the English names, so nothing you save changes.
settings.regions.label: Bird Regions
settings.regions.hint: Selects which biogeographic regions to include in the species autocomplete (Ctrl+Shift+R), and the default list of species Kestrel identifies from when you analyze a folder (you can override it per analysis). Multiple regions show their union. Species outside the selected regions are hidden from the combobox.
settings.showScientificNames.label: Show scientific names
settings.showScientificNames.hint: When on, the Latin binomial appears in italics under each species pill (scene dialog and timeline cards), and family pills show the scientific family name.
settings.rating.veryStrict: Very Strict — only the sharpest images reach 4–5 stars
settings.rating.veryLenient: Very Lenient — most rewarding; lowest bar for 4–5 stars
settings.rating.hint: Controls how quality scores are converted to star ratings. Each profile uses fixed quality-score thresholds — stricter profiles require a higher score to earn 4 or 5 stars. Changes take effect immediately for loaded folders.
settings.rating.dragHint: Drag a star to move the score it needs. Arrow keys nudge by 0.01.
settings.rawPreviewCache.label: Save RAW previews for faster loading
settings.rawPreviewCache.hint: Keep full-size RAW previews in the .kestrel/culling_TMP folder so later loads are faster. Turn off to save disk space; previews are then made again each time.
settings.expComp.label: Preview exposure compensation
settings.expComp.hint: Display only: how strongly Kestrel's calculated exposure boost is applied to preview imagery (grid & scene-dialog export thumbnails and the RAW zoom). 0% shows the uncorrected export; 100% matches the processed bird crop. The same slider is in the scene viewer. Does not affect analysis or the baked crop.
settings.autoSave.label: Auto-Save Changes
settings.autoSave.hint: Automatically save ratings, tags, and scene changes. When disabled, you'll see a Save/Revert workflow.
settings.qualityModel.label: Quality scorer
settings.qualityModel.siglip: Newer sharpness model (added in Arctic Tern)
settings.qualityModel.hint: Both scores are computed during analysis (analysis version 3.0) and stored, so switching is instant — no re-analysis. Both judge focus/sharpness only, not whether a photo is "good". The original model is the default again from Arctic Tern (FP 1); the newer model is kept so you can compare. Folders analysed before 3.0 only have the legacy score until upgraded.
settings.smartSearch.label: Smart search: index whole frames
settings.smartSearch.hint: Bird crops are always indexed for smart search. This also indexes each photo's whole frame so scene queries work ("bird on a wire", "two birds", "wide landscape"). Adds about 0.1–0.2 seconds per photo on the CPU.
settings.rawEmbedded.label: Fast RAW analysis: use the camera’s embedded JPEG
settings.rawEmbedded.hint: Analyses the JPEG preview stored inside each RAW file instead of decoding the sensor data. Much faster per photo; the sharpness score is largely unaffected, but exposure/highlight recovery is skipped and quality depends on the preview size your camera writes (some older bodies embed only a small one). RAWs without a usable preview are still decoded. Applies to analyses started after you change it, on this computer only — Cloud Compute always decodes RAW.
settings.towerDevice.label: Species model device (advanced)
settings.towerDevice.hint: Where the species and search models run when GPU analysis is on. Auto: GPU on Windows, CPU on macOS, where the GPU path does not support these models. Applies to the next analysis.
settings.eg.label: Enhanced GPU performance {tag}
settings.eg.hint: Enhanced GPU Performance uses extra GPU software made for your graphics hardware to speed up analysis. Setup downloads that software from Windows and tests Kestrel’s models on your computer. If it fails, Kestrel uses standard GPU acceleration.
settings.eg.reportPrompt: Setup did not finish. Would you like to send a bug report? It includes your recent log, which lists the GPU options Windows offered, so we can improve support for your hardware.
settings.impact.label: Kestrel's Impact
settings.impact.hint: Total number of photos analyzed by Kestrel on this computer.
settings.analytics.label: Share anonymous usage analytics
settings.analytics.hint: Helps improve Kestrel. No filenames, paths, or images are ever shared. You can change this at any time.
settings.crash.label: Send crash reports
settings.crash.hint: Automatically send a report if Kestrel crashes, so we can find and fix the problem. No filenames, paths, or images are ever shared.
settings.qf.label: Quality feedback
settings.qf.hint: Sort a few bird crops by sharpness to help improve Kestrel. Anonymous.

analyze.q.subjects: What subjects does this shoot contain?
analyze.q.subjects.help: Including other wildlife names 1,200+ non-bird species — squirrels, deer, bears and more. This has a small impact on total processing time.
analyze.q.species: Should Kestrel identify the bird species?
analyze.q.species.help: Kestrel names each bird from the world's ~11,000 bird species, narrowed to the region below. Skipping it makes analysis faster; finding your subjects and scoring their quality work exactly the same either way.
analyze.q.species.regionHint: A narrower region list makes identification more accurate. Change your default regions in Settings → Species & Region.
analyze.q.maxSubjects: How many subjects should Kestrel analyze in each image?
analyze.q.maxSubjects.help: Every extra subject adds processing time. Lower this for flock shots where you only care about the closest few birds.
analyze.gpu.label: Use GPU when available
analyze.gpu.hint: Speeds up detection and species identification on your GPU. Turn off if your GPU is unstable.
analyze.prefetch.label: Photos to load ahead
analyze.prefetch.hint: How many photos to load in advance so analysis keeps moving (1–5). Lower this if your computer slows down too much during analysis.
analyze.retryErrored.label: Re-attempt errored images
analyze.retryErrored.hint: For any queued folder containing images previously marked as errored, drop those rows and re-run analysis on them. Other already-analyzed images are not touched.
analyze.detectionModel.label: Detection model
analyze.detectionModel.hint: Accurate is the right choice for almost every shoot. Fast uses a smaller model that finishes sooner but misses distant and partly-hidden birds.
analyze.detectionConfidence.label: Detection confidence
analyze.detectionConfidence.hint: How sure Kestrel must be that it found an animal before analyzing it (0.10–0.99). Lower values find more subjects.
analyze.detectionConfidence.warning: ⚠ Kestrel suggests 0.15. Higher values miss real subjects.
analyze.exposure.label: Exposure correction
analyze.exposure.hint: Controls how strongly Kestrel corrects bird exposure in the analyzed crops. Balanced is recommended for most images.
analyze.sceneTime.label: Seconds between shots in one scene
analyze.sceneTime.hint: Images captured within this many seconds of each other are treated as the same burst/scene.
analyze.sceneBreak.label: Start a new scene after a pause of (seconds)
analyze.sceneBreak.hint: Forces a scene break whenever this much time passes between two shots, even if they look alike — useful when a long session against the same background would otherwise become one huge scene. 0 turns it off.
analyze.thumbnailWidth.label: Thumbnail width (px)
analyze.thumbnailWidth.hint: Size of the cached analysis thumbnails, in pixels on the longest side. Larger looks sharper but uses more space in the .kestrel folder.
analyze.thumbnailJpeg.label: Thumbnail JPEG compression
analyze.thumbnailJpeg.hint: 0.75 means 75% JPEG quality. Lower values reduce file size with more visible compression artifacts.
analyze.summaryEmpty: Check folders in the queue builder to add them.
analyze.reanalyze.label: Re-analyze fully-analyzed folders
analyze.reanalyze.hint: Will erase user data (ratings, decisions, scene names) for those folders.

folderActions.upgradeReanalyzeDefault: re-analyse this folder to use analysis version 3.0.
folderActions.upgradeConfirm:
Upgrade “{name}” to analysis version 3.0?

Kestrel re-reads the bird crops and preview images it already saved (no RAW decoding) to update species IDs, add the new sharpness score and build the smart-search index. Your culling decisions, star ratings and edited tags are not changed, and the database is backed up first. Runs on this computer only (uses the GPU when enabled).
